newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says may convert Belgian plant.
newsitem.headline: Renault says may convert Belgian plant.

text.p: Renault SA chairman Louis Schweitzer said on Wednesday he was ready to discuss with Belgian trade unions "converting" the plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels which his company has announced it plans to close.
He also said he had assured French Prime Minister Alain Juppe that Renault would fully respect French, Belgian and European law.

Renault's decision to close Vilvoorde from June, with the loss of 3,100 direct jobs, has triggered widespread protests in Belgium, political anger in both countries and the first signs of a boycott of Renault vehicles in Belgium.

"I told the prime minister that Renault wants to start consultations immediately with representatives of the personnel at Vilvoorde about accompanying measures and the possibilities of converting the factory," Schweitzer said.
Juppe summoned him to his office after President Jacques Chirac said he was shocked by the methods used by Renault to announce the factory closure.

The company chairman said he would present restructuring plans, which also involve 2,764 job losses in France this year, to Renault's works council on Thursday and hold a special European works council meeting, including Belgian staff representatives, on March 11.
